Well-posedness results for a generalized Klein-Gordon-Schrödinger system

Hartmut Pecher
Fakultät für Mathematik und Naturwissenschaften
Bergische Universität Wuppertal
Gaußstr. 20
42119 Wuppertal
Germany
e-mail pecher@math.uni-wuppertal.de
Abstract.

We consider the Klein-Gordon-Schrödinger system i​∂tψ+Δ​ψ=ϕ2​ψ−ϕ​ψi\partial_{t}\psi+\Delta\psi=\phi^{2}\psi-\phi\psi , (□+1)​ϕ=−2​|ψ|2​ϕ+|ψ|2(\Box+1)\phi=-2|\psi|^{2}\phi+|\psi|^{2} with additional cubic terms and Cauchy data ψ⁡(0)=ψ0∈Hs​(ℝn),ϕ⁡(0)=ϕ0∈Hk​(ℝn),(∂tϕ)​(0)=ϕ1∈Hk−1​(ℝn)\psi(0)=\psi_{0}\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{n})\,,\,\phi(0)=\phi_{0}\in H^{k}(\mathbb{R}^{n})\,,\,(\partial_{t}\phi)(0)=\phi_{1}\in H^{k-1}(\mathbb{R}^{n}) in space dimensions n=2n=2 and n=3n=3 . We prove local existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence on the data in Bourgain-Klainerman-Machedon spaces for low regularity data, e.g. for s=−18s=-\frac{1}{8}, k=38+ϵk=\frac{3}{8}+\epsilon in the case n=2n=2 and s=0s=0 , k=12+ϵk=\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon in the case n=3n=3. Global well-posedness in energy space is also obtained as a special case. Moreover, we show ”unconditional” uniqueness in the space ψ∈C0​([0,T],Hs)\psi\in C^{0}([0,T],H^{s}), ϕ∈C0​([0,T],Hs+12)∩C1​([0,T],Hs−12)\phi\in C^{0}([0,T],H^{s+\frac{1}{2}})\cap C^{1}([0,T],H^{s-\frac{1}{2}}), if s>322s>\frac{3}{22} for n=2n=2 and s>12s>\frac{1}{2} for n=3n=3.

††footnotetext: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: 35Q55, 35L70
Key words and phrases: Klein-Gordon-Schrödinger, local well-posedness, unconditional uniqueness

1. Introduction

Consider the Klein-Gordon-Schrödinger system

i​∂tψ+Δ​ψ\displaystyle i\partial_{t}\psi+\Delta\psi =ϕ2​ψ−ϕ​ψ\displaystyle=\phi^{2}\psi-\phi\psi (1)
(□+1)​ϕ\displaystyle(\Box+1)\phi =−2​|ψ|2​ϕ+|ψ|2\displaystyle=-2|\psi|^{2}\phi+|\psi|^{2} (2)

with Cauchy data

ψ⁡(0)=ψ0∈Hs​(ℝn),ϕ⁡(0)=ϕ0∈Hk​(ℝn),(∂tϕ)​(0)=ϕ1∈Hk−1​(ℝn)\psi(0)=\psi_{0}\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{n})\,,\,\phi(0)=\phi_{0}\in H^{k}(\mathbb{R}^{n})\,,\,(\partial_{t}\phi)(0)=\phi_{1}\in H^{k-1}(\mathbb{R}^{n}) (3)

in space dimensions n=2n=2 and n=3n=3 , where □=∂t2−Δ\Box=\partial_{t}^{2}-\Delta .

This system is a generalization of the classical Klein-Gordon-Schrödinger system (KGS) with Yukawa interaction of a complex nucleon field ψ\psi and a real meson field ϕ\phi. The classical KGS system without the cubic nonlinearities was considered extensively in the literature. We are primarily interested in well-posedness results for data with low regularity.

For the classical KGS system in the case n=2n=2 local well-posedness in Bourgain-Klainerman-Machedon type spaces (BKM spaces) holds for s>−14s>-\frac{1}{4} , k≥−12k\geq-\frac{1}{2}, k−2​s<32k-2s<\frac{3}{2} , k−2<s<k+1k-2<s<k+1 . These conditions are sharp up to the endpoints. Uniqueness in the larger natural solution spaces ψ∈C0​([0,T],Hs)\psi\in C^{0}([0,T],H^{s}) , ϕ∈C0​([0,T],Hk)∩C1​([0,T],Hk−1)\phi\in C^{0}([0,T],H^{k})\cap C^{1}([0,T],H^{k-1}) (”unconditional uniqueness”) holds, if s,k≥0s,k\geq 0 . The solutions exist globally (in t), if s≥0s\geq 0 , s−12≤k<s+12s-\frac{1}{2}\leq k<s+\frac{1}{2}. These results were shown by the author [5].

In the case n=3n=3 local well-posedness in BKM spaces holds under the same conditions in ss and kk except that we have to assume k>−12k>-\frac{1}{2}. This is also sharp up to the endpoints. The unconditional uniqueness result holds for s=k=0s=k=0 , in which case also global well-posedness is true. This was proven by the author in [6].

The proofs are based on the results by Bejenaru and Herr [4] in the case n=3n=3 and Bejenaru-Herr-Holmer-Tataru [3] in the case n=2n=2.

In the more general case (1),(2) with additional cubic interactions much less is known. For dimension n=2n=2 Shi-Li-Wang [8] proved global well-posedness in energy space s=k=1s=k=1 using Kato type smoothing estimates for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation.

In the present paper this result can be improved by using BKM type spaces and the methods in the author’s paper [5]. We obtain local well-posedness (existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence on the data) for s>−18s>-\frac{1}{8} , k>38k>\frac{3}{8} and s<min⁡(2​k−14,k+12)s<\min(2k-\frac{1}{4},k+\frac{1}{2}) , s>max⁡(k−12,k−32)s>\max(\frac{k-1}{2},k-\frac{3}{2}) , e.g. s=−18+s=-\frac{1}{8}+ , k=38+k=\frac{3}{8}+ , in BKM spaces, which are subsets of the natural solution spaces ψ∈C0​([0,T],Hs)\psi\in C^{0}([0,T],H^{s}) , ϕ∈C0​([0,T],Hk)∩C1​([0,T],Hk−1)\phi\in C^{0}([0,T],H^{k})\cap C^{1}([0,T],H^{k-1}) . ”Unconditional” uniqueness in these latter spaces is shown for s>322s>\frac{3}{22} and (for simplicity) k=s+12k=s+\frac{1}{2} . Global well-posedness in energy space easily follows as a byproduct. We rely mainly on the results in [5] combined with bilinear estimates for BKM spaces for the Klein-Gordon part by d’Ancona, Foschi and Selberg [1]. We apply only an appropriate version of the contraction mapping principle which also has the advantage that it is well-known that the solution depends continuously on the data.

In the case n=3n=3 Ran-Shi [7] proved two main results, first well-posedness in energy space s=k=1s=k=1 by considering atomic solution spaces U2U^{2} and V2V^{2} and the perturbed linear Schrödinger equation i∂t+(Δ+ϕ)ψ=0i\partial_{t}+(\Delta+\phi)\psi=0 . Secondly local well-posedness holds in the case s>12s>\frac{1}{2} , k=1k=1 , which improves earlier results by Shi-Wang-Li-Wang [9].

In the present paper we use the standard contraction mapping principle and obtain local well-posedness in BKM type spaces for s≥0s\geq 0 , k>12k>\frac{1}{2} , s<min⁡(2​k−12,k+12)s<\min(2k-\frac{1}{2},k+\frac{1}{2}) , s>max⁡(k−12,k−32)s>\max(\frac{k-1}{2},k-\frac{3}{2}) , especially for s=0s=0 , k=12+k=\frac{1}{2}+. Unconditional uniqueness holds for s>12s>\frac{1}{2} , k=s+12k=s+\frac{1}{2} . Global well-posedness in energy space also follows easily.

In fact, it is well-known that the system (1),(2) satisfies mass conservation

‖ψ‖L2=‖ψ0‖L2\|\psi\|_{L^{2}}=\|\psi_{0}\|_{L^{2}}

and energy conservation

E⁡(t)≡‖∇ψ‖L22+12​(‖∂tϕ‖L22+‖∇ϕ‖L22+‖ϕ‖L22)+2​‖ψ​ϕ‖L22−∫ϕ​|ψ|2​𝑑x=E⁡(0).E(t)\equiv\|\nabla\psi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}(\|\partial_{t}\phi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\phi\|_{L^{2}}^{2})+2\|\psi\phi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}-\int\phi|\psi|^{2}dx=E(0)\,.

One easily shows that, if ψ0∈H1\psi_{0}\in H^{1} , ϕ0∈H1\phi_{0}\in H^{1} , ϕ1∈L2\phi_{1}\in L^{2} , then

E(0)≤c0(∥ψ0∥H1,∥ϕ0∥H1,∥ϕ1|L2).E(0)\leq c_{0}(\|\psi_{0}\|_{H^{1}},\|\phi_{0}\|_{H^{1}},\|\phi_{1}|_{L^{2}})\,.

Moreover

|∫ϕ​|ψ|2​𝑑x|\displaystyle|\int\phi|\psi|^{2}dx| ≤‖ϕ‖L6​‖|ψ|12‖L12​‖|ψ|32‖L43\displaystyle\leq\|\phi\|_{L^{6}}\||\psi|^{\frac{1}{2}}\|_{L^{12}}\||\psi|^{\frac{3}{2}}\|_{L^{\frac{4}{3}}}
≲‖∇ϕ‖L2​‖∇ψ‖L212​‖ψ‖L232\displaystyle\lesssim\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^{2}}\|\nabla\psi\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\|\psi\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{3}{2}}
≤14​(‖∇ϕ‖L22+‖∇ψ‖L22)+c​‖ψ‖L26,\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{4}(\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\nabla\psi\|_{L^{2}}^{2})+c\|\psi\|_{L^{2}}^{6}\,,

so that

‖∇ψ‖L22+12​(‖∂tϕ‖L22+‖∇ϕ‖L22+‖ϕ‖L22)≤E⁡(0)+14​(‖∇ϕ‖L22+‖∇ψ‖L22)+c​‖ψ0‖L26,\|\nabla\psi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}(\|\partial_{t}\phi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\phi\|_{L^{2}}^{2})\leq E(0)+\frac{1}{4}(\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\nabla\psi\|_{L^{2}}^{2})+c\|\psi_{0}\|_{L^{2}}^{6}\,,

which implies the a-priori bound

‖∇ψ‖L22+‖∂tϕ‖L22+‖∇ϕ‖L22+‖ϕ‖L22≤c1​(‖ψ0‖H1,‖ϕ0‖H1,‖ϕ1‖L2).\|\nabla\psi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\partial_{t}\phi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\phi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\leq c_{1}(\|\psi_{0}\|_{H^{1}},\|\phi_{0}\|_{H^{1}},\|\phi_{1}\|_{L^{2}})\,.

Thus, if we have a unique local solution in [0,T][0,T] for data ψ0∈H1\psi_{0}\in H^{1} , ϕ0∈H1\phi_{0}\in H^{1} , ϕ1∈L2\phi_{1}\in L^{2} with T=T⁡(‖ψ0‖H1,‖ϕ0‖H1,‖ϕ1‖L2CLOSET=T(\|\psi_{0}\|_{H^{1}},\|\phi_{0}\|_{H^{1}},\|\phi_{1}\|_{L^{2}} , this solution can easily be extended globally in time.

We only use the standard Bourgain spaces Xm,bX^{m,b} for the Schrödinger equation, which are defined as the completion of 𝒮⁡(ℝn×ℝ){\mathcal{S}}(\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}) with respect to the norm

‖f‖Xm,b:=‖⟨ξ⟩m​⟨τ+|ξ|2⟩b​f^​(ξ,τ)‖Lξ​τ2.\|f\|_{X^{m,b}}:=\|\langle\xi\rangle^{m}\langle\tau+|\xi|^{2}\rangle^{b}\widehat{f}(\xi,\tau)\|_{L^{2}_{\xi\tau}}\,.

Similarly the Klainerman-Machedon spaces X±m.bX^{m.b}_{\pm} for the equation

i​∂tn±∓(−Δ+1)12​n±=0i\partial_{t}n_{\pm}\mp(-\Delta+1)^{\frac{1}{2}}n_{\pm}=0

are the completion of 𝒮⁡(ℝn×ℝ){\mathcal{S}}(\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}) with respect to the norm

‖f‖X±m,b:=‖⟨ξ⟩m​⟨τ±|ξ|⟩b​f^​(ξ,τ)‖Lξ​τ2.\|f\|_{X_{\pm}^{m,b}}:=\|\langle\xi\rangle^{m}\langle\tau\pm|\xi|\rangle^{b}\widehat{f}(\xi,\tau)\|_{L^{2}_{\xi\tau}}\,.

For a given time interval II we define

∥f∥Xm,b​(I):=inff~|I=f∥f~∥Xm,b\|f\|_{X^{m,b}(I)}:=\inf_{\tilde{f}_{|I}=f}\|\tilde{f}\|_{X^{m,b}}

and similarly ‖f‖X±m,b​(I)\|f\|_{X^{m,b}_{\pm}(I)} .

We now formulate our main results.

Theorem 1.1.

(Local well-posedness) In the case n=2n=2 assume

s≥−18,k>38,s<min⁡(2​k−14,k+12),s>max⁡(k−12,k−32).s\geq-\frac{1}{8}\,,\,k>\frac{3}{8}\,,\,s<\min(2k-\frac{1}{4},k+\frac{1}{2})\,,\,s>\max(\frac{k-1}{2},k-\frac{3}{2})\,.

In the case n=3n=3 assume

s≥0,k>12,s<min⁡(2​k−12,k+12),s>max⁡(k−12,k−32).s\geq 0\,,\,k>\frac{1}{2}\,,\,s<\min(2k-\frac{1}{2},k+\frac{1}{2})\,,\,s>\max(\frac{k-1}{2},k-\frac{3}{2})\,.

The Cauchy problem (1),(2),(3) has a unique local solution

ψ∈Xs,12+​[0,T],ϕ∈X+k,12+​[0,T]+X−k,12+​[0,T],\psi\in X^{s,\frac{1}{2}+}[0,T]\,,\,\phi\in X^{k,\frac{1}{2}+}_{+}[0,T]+X^{k,\frac{1}{2}+}_{-}[0,T]\,,
∂tϕ∈X+k−1,12+​[0,T]+X−k−1,12+​[0,T],\partial_{t}\phi\in X^{k-1,\frac{1}{2}+}_{+}[0,T]+X^{k-1,\frac{1}{2}+}_{-}[0,T]\,,

where T=T⁡(‖ψ0‖Hs,‖ϕ0‖Hk,‖ψ1‖Hk−1)T=T(\|\psi_{0}\|_{H^{s}},\|\phi_{0}\|_{H^{k}},\|\psi_{1}\|_{H^{k-1}}) . This solution fufills

ψ∈C0​([0,T],Hs),ϕ∈C0​([0,T],Hk)∩C1​([0,T],Hk−1).\psi\in C^{0}([0,T],H^{s})\,,\,\phi\in C^{0}([0,T],H^{k})\cap C^{1}([0,T],H^{k-1})\,.

Remark: The solution depends continuously on the initial data and persistence of higher regularity holds. This is a standard fact for solutions obtained by a contraction argument as in our case.

Theorem 1.2.

(Unconditional uniqueness) If we assume k=s+12k=s+\frac{1}{2} , and s>322s>\frac{3}{22} in the case n=2n=2 and s>12s>\frac{1}{2} in the case n=3n=3 then there exists a unique solution of (1),(2),(3) in the space

ψ∈C0​([0,T],Hs),ϕ∈C0​([0,T],Hk)∩C1​([0,T],Hk−1).\psi\in C^{0}([0,T],H^{s})\,,\,\phi\in C^{0}([0,T],H^{k})\cap C^{1}([0,T],H^{k-1})\,.

2. Preliminaries

We transform the KGS into an equivalent first order (in t) system as follows. Defining

ϕ±=ϕ±i​(−Δ+1)−12​∂tϕ\phi_{\pm}=\phi\pm i(-\Delta+1)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\partial_{t}\phi

we obtain the system

i​∂tψ+Δ​ψ\displaystyle i\partial_{t}\psi+\Delta\psi =(ϕ++ϕ−)2​ψ−(ϕ++ϕ−)​ψ\displaystyle=(\phi_{+}+\phi_{-})^{2}\psi-(\phi_{+}+\phi_{-})\psi
i​∂tϕ±∓(−Δ+1)12​ϕ±\displaystyle i\partial_{t}\phi_{\pm}\mp(-\Delta+1)^{\frac{1}{2}}\phi_{\pm} =±(−Δ+1)−12​(−2​|ψ|2​(ϕ++ϕ−)+|ψ|2)\displaystyle=\pm(-\Delta+1)^{-\frac{1}{2}}(-2|\psi|^{2}(\phi_{+}+\phi_{-})+|\psi|^{2})

with data

ψ⁡(0)=ψ0∈Hs,ϕ±​(0)=ϕ0±i​(−Δ+1)−12​ϕ1∈Hk.\psi(0)=\psi_{0}\in H^{s}\,,\,\phi_{\pm}(0)=\phi_{0}\pm i(-\Delta+1)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\phi_{1}\in H^{k}\,.

Fundamental for the proof of the multilinear estimates are also the following bilnear estimates in Klainerman-Machedon spaces spaces which were proven by d’Ancona, Foschi and Selberg in the cases n=2n=2 in [1] and n=3n=3 in [2] in a more general form which include many limit cases which we do not need.

Proposition 2.1.

Let n=2n=2 or n=3n=3. The estimate

∥uv∥X±−s0,−b0≲∥u∥Xs1,b1±1∥v∥Xs2,b2±2\|uv\|_{X_{\pm}^{-s_{0},-b_{0}}}\lesssim\|u\|_{X^{s_{1},b_{1}}_{\pm_{1}}}\|v\|_{X^{s_{2},b_{2}}_{\pm_{2}}}

holds, where ±,±1,±2\pm,\pm_{1},\pm_{2} denote independent signs, provided the following conditions are satisfied:

b0,b1,b2≥0\displaystyle b_{0},b_{1},b_{2}\geq 0
b0+b1+b2>12\displaystyle b_{0}+b_{1}+b_{2}>\frac{1}{2}
s0+s1+s2>n+12−(b0+b1+b2)\displaystyle s_{0}+s_{1}+s_{2}>\frac{n+1}{2}-(b_{0}+b_{1}+b_{2})
s0+s1+s2>n2−(b0+b1)\displaystyle s_{0}+s_{1}+s_{2}>\frac{n}{2}-(b_{0}+b_{1})
s0+s1+s2>n2−(b0+b2)\displaystyle s_{0}+s_{1}+s_{2}>\frac{n}{2}-(b_{0}+b_{2})
s0+s1+s2>n2−(b1+b2)\displaystyle s_{0}+s_{1}+s_{2}>\frac{n}{2}-(b_{1}+b_{2})
s0+s1+s2>n−12−b0\displaystyle s_{0}+s_{1}+s_{2}>\frac{n-1}{2}-b_{0}
s0+s1+s2>n−12−b1\displaystyle s_{0}+s_{1}+s_{2}>\frac{n-1}{2}-b_{1}
s0+s1+s2>n−12−b2\displaystyle s_{0}+s_{1}+s_{2}>\frac{n-1}{2}-b_{2}
s0+s1+s2>n+14\displaystyle s_{0}+s_{1}+s_{2}>\frac{n+1}{4}
(s0+b0)+2​s1+2​s2>n2\displaystyle(s_{0}+b_{0})+2s_{1}+2s_{2}>\frac{n}{2}
2​s0+(s1+b1)+2​s2>n2\displaystyle 2s_{0}+(s_{1}+b_{1})+2s_{2}>\frac{n}{2}
2​s0+2​s1+(s2+b2)>n2\displaystyle 2s_{0}+2s_{1}+(s_{2}+b_{2})>\frac{n}{2}
s1+s2≥0\displaystyle s_{1}+s_{2}\geq 0
s0+s2≥0\displaystyle s_{0}+s_{2}\geq 0
s0+s1≥0.\displaystyle s_{0}+s_{1}\geq 0\,.

3. The case n=2n=2

We now prove the necessary bi- and trilinear estimates.

Proposition 3.1.

Let s>−12s>-\frac{1}{2} , k>38k>\frac{3}{8} and s<min⁡(2​k−14,k+12)s<\min(2k-\frac{1}{4},k+\frac{1}{2}) . Then the following estimate holds for sufficiently small ϵ>0\epsilon>0 :

∥ϕ1ϕ2ψ∥Xs,−12+2​ϵ≲∥ϕ1∥Xk,12+ϵ±1∥ϕ2∥Xk,12+ϵ±2∥ψ∥Xs,12+ϵ.\|\phi_{1}\phi_{2}\psi\|_{X^{s,-\frac{1}{2}+2\epsilon}}\lesssim\|\phi_{1}\|_{X^{k,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}_{\pm_{1}}}\|\phi_{2}\|_{X^{k,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}_{\pm_{2}}}\|\psi\|_{X^{s,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}}\,. (4)

We need the following lemmas for its proof.

Lemma 3.1.

The following estimates hold for k>38k>\frac{3}{8} :

∥ϕ1ϕ2∥X±2​k−54−,12−≲∥ϕ1∥Xk,12+ϵ±1∥ϕ2∥Xk,12+ϵ±2,\|\phi_{1}\phi_{2}\|_{X^{2k-\frac{5}{4}-,\frac{1}{2}-}_{\pm}}\lesssim\|\phi_{1}\|_{X^{k,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}_{\pm_{1}}}\|\phi_{2}\|_{X^{k,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}_{\pm_{2}}}\,, (5)

if k≤34k\leq\frac{3}{4} , and

∥ϕ1ϕ2∥X±k−12−,12−≲∥ϕ1∥Xk,12+ϵ±1∥ϕ2∥Xk,12+ϵ±2,\|\phi_{1}\phi_{2}\|_{X^{k-\frac{1}{2}-,\frac{1}{2}-}_{\pm}}\lesssim\|\phi_{1}\|_{X^{k,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}_{\pm_{1}}}\|\phi_{2}\|_{X^{k,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}_{\pm_{2}}}\,, (6)

if k>34k>\frac{3}{4} .

Proof.

Let ξ0=ξ1+ξ2\xi_{0}=\xi_{1}+\xi_{2} , τ0=τ1+τ2\tau_{0}=\tau_{1}+\tau_{2} , where ξj∈ℝn,τj∈ℝ\xi_{j}\in\mathbb{R}^{n},\tau_{j}\in\mathbb{R} . The following elementary estimate holds:

|τ0±|ξ0||\displaystyle|\tau_{0}\pm|\xi_{0}|| =|τ1+τ2±1|ξ1|±2|ξ2|∓1|ξ1|±2|ξ2|±|ξ0||\displaystyle=|\tau_{1}+\tau_{2}\pm_{1}|\xi_{1}|\pm_{2}|\xi_{2}|\mp_{1}|\xi_{1}|\pm_{2}|\xi_{2}|\pm|\xi_{0}||
≲|τ1±1|ξ1||+|τ2±2|ξ2||+max(|ξ1|,|ξ2|).\displaystyle\lesssim|\tau_{1}\pm_{1}|\xi_{1}||+|\tau_{2}\pm_{2}|\xi_{2}||+\max(|\xi_{1}|,|\xi_{2}|)\,. (7)

By (7) we may reduce (5) to the estimates

‖ϕ1​ϕ2‖X±2​k−54−,0\displaystyle\|\phi_{1}\phi_{2}\|_{X^{2k-\frac{5}{4}-,0}_{\pm}} ≲∥ϕ1∥Xk−12+,12+ϵ±1∥ϕ2∥Xk,12+ϵ±2,\displaystyle\lesssim\|\phi_{1}\|_{X^{k-\frac{1}{2}+,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}_{\pm_{1}}}\|\phi_{2}\|_{X^{k,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}_{\pm_{2}}}\,, (8)

For (9) similarly we choose s0=54−2​k+s_{0}=\frac{5}{4}-2k+ , s1=s2=ks_{1}=s_{2}=k , b0=b1=0b_{0}=b_{1}=0 , b2=12+ϵb_{2}=\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon , so that s0+s1+s2=54+s_{0}+s_{1}+s_{2}=\frac{5}{4}+ , s1+s2=2​k≥34s_{1}+s_{2}=2k\geq\frac{3}{4} , s0+s2=54−k>0s_{0}+s_{2}=\frac{5}{4}-k>0 .

By (7) we reduce (6) to the estimates

‖ϕ1​ϕ2‖X±k−12−,0\displaystyle\|\phi_{1}\phi_{2}\|_{X^{k-\frac{1}{2}-,0}_{\pm}} ≲∥ϕ1∥Xk−12+,12+ϵ±1∥ϕ2∥Xk,12+ϵ±2,\displaystyle\lesssim\|\phi_{1}\|_{X^{k-\frac{1}{2}+,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}_{\pm_{1}}}\|\phi_{2}\|_{X^{k,\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon}_{\pm_{2}}}\,, (10)

For (23) we choose s0=14+2​ϵs_{0}=\frac{1}{4}+2\epsilon , s1=kj−12+s_{1}=k_{j}-\frac{1}{2}+ , s2=1−kj+1s_{2}=1-k_{j+1}, b0=0b_{0}=0 , b1=12+b_{1}=\frac{1}{2}+ , b2=12−b_{2}=\frac{1}{2}- , thus s0+s1+s2=34+2​ϵ+kj−kj+1+>34s_{0}+s_{1}+s_{2}=\frac{3}{4}+2\epsilon+k_{j}-k_{j+1}+>\frac{3}{4} , if kj+1=kj+2​ϵk_{j+1}=k_{j}+2\epsilon . Proof of Theorem 1.1.

By standard arguments the claimed local well-posedness in Theorem 1.1 is a consequence of Propositions 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3. ∎

Next, we prove the unconditional well-posedness result.

Proof of Theorem 1.2.

As in the two-dimensional case we obtain

Lemma 4.5.

Let 13<s≤23\frac{1}{3}<s\leq\frac{2}{3} . Then we have

ψ\displaystyle\psi ∈X3​s−2,1​[0,T]∩Xs,0​[0,T]⊂X2​s−1−,12+​[0,T],\displaystyle\in X^{3s-2,1}[0,T]\cap X^{s,0}[0,T]\subset X^{2s-1-,\frac{1}{2}+}[0,T]\,,
ϕ±\displaystyle\phi_{\pm} ∈X±3​s−32,1​[0,T]∩X±s+12,0​[0,T]⊂X±2​s−12−,12+​[0,T].\displaystyle\in X^{3s-\frac{3}{2},1}_{\pm}[0,T]\cap X^{s+\frac{1}{2},0}_{\pm}[0,T]\subset X^{2s-\frac{1}{2}-,\frac{1}{2}+}_{\pm}[0,T]\,.
Proof.

We use the same notation as in the proof of Lemma 3.6, i.e. 1r=12−l2\frac{1}{r}=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{l}{2}, 1p=12−s+123\frac{1}{p}=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{s+\frac{1}{2}}{3} , 1q=12−s3\frac{1}{q}=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{s}{3} , so that 1r=2p+1q=76−s<1\frac{1}{r}=\frac{2}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=\frac{7}{6}-s<1 , if s>16s>\frac{1}{6} and l=3​s−2≤0l=3s-2\leq 0 , if s≤23s\leq\frac{2}{3} . Moreover 1r∗=12−m3\frac{1}{r^{*}}=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{m}{3} , 1r∗=1p+2q=43−s<1\frac{1}{r^{*}}=\frac{1}{p}+\frac{2}{q}=\frac{4}{3}-s<1 , if s>13s>\frac{1}{3} , and m=3​s−52≤0m=3s-\frac{5}{2}\leq 0 for s≤56s\leq\frac{5}{6} , This gives the necessary estimates for the cubic nonlinearities exactly as in Lemma 3.6. The quadratic nonlinearities are easily treated in the same way. ∎

Finally, in order to obtain the claimed unconditional uniqueness of Theorem 1.2 it suffices to consider the case s=12+ϵs=\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon . By Lemma 4.5 we obtain ψ∈X0,12+​[0,T]\psi\in X^{0,\frac{1}{2}+}[0,T] and ϕ∈X12+,12+​[0,T]\phi\in X^{\frac{1}{2}+,\frac{1}{2}+}[0,T] . But in these spaces the uniqueness holds by Theorem 1.1. ∎
